units.title: Number: place value, signed numbers and powers of 10
units.description: Read, order and compare large and signed numbers, then use powers of 10 to make reliable changes to whole numbers and decimals.
units.generationNotes: Use short, realistic numerical contexts. Make the direction of a multiply or divide by 10, 100 or 1,000 explicit. Include a number-line or temperature context for signed numbers. Each explanation must show the calculation or comparison clearly; never say that a decimal point simply moves without explaining place value.

objectives.text: Read, write, order and compare large numbers up to one million.
Recognise and use positive and negative numbers.
Multiply and divide whole numbers and decimals by 10, 100 and 1,000.
Use multiplication facts and make connections with division facts.

units.title: Number: formulae, squares and order of operations
units.description: Turn a word rule into a calculation, work with squares, and follow the correct order when a calculation has more than one operation.
units.generationNotes: Use everyday formulae such as total cost, perimeter or pay. Include one-step and two-step formulae, but do not introduce algebra beyond the stated skill. For order of operations, use brackets only where they clarify a Level 1 calculation and show each step in the explanation.

objectives.text: Use simple formulae expressed in words for one-step and 2-step operations.
Calculate the squares of one-digit and 2-digit numbers.
Follow the order of precedence of operators.

units.title: Number: fractions and mixed numbers
units.description: Read, order and compare common fractions and mixed numbers, then find a fraction of a whole-number quantity or measurement.
units.generationNotes: Use quantities that divide exactly unless the purpose is comparison. Include one mixed-number comparison and one fraction-of-a-measurement question. Show the method in explanations, for example dividing by the denominator then multiplying by the numerator, rather than offering an unexplained answer.

objectives.text: Read, write, order and compare common fractions and mixed numbers.
Find fractions of whole-number quantities and measurements.

units.title: Number: decimals, calculation and estimation
units.description: Order decimals, calculate with money-style values, and use rounding to make a sensible estimate or check an answer.
units.generationNotes: Use decimals to no more than the stated precision. Include one addition or subtraction, one multiplication or division, and one estimate/check. Keep monetary contexts fictional and make clear when an estimate is appropriate rather than an exact final amount.

objectives.text: Read, write, order and compare decimals up to 3 decimal places.
Add, subtract, multiply and divide decimals up to 2 decimal places.
Approximate by rounding to a whole number, one decimal place and 2 decimal places.

units.title: Number: percentages, equivalence, ratio and proportion
units.description: Compare whole-number percentages, calculate common percentage changes, and connect fractions, decimals, percentages, simple ratios and direct proportion.
units.generationNotes: Cover a percentage of a quantity or a 5% multiple increase/decrease, a fraction-decimal-percentage equivalence, and a simple ratio or direct-proportion situation. Use exact, checkable values. Do not introduce compound interest or percentages not supported by the Level 1 scope.

objectives.text: Read, write, order and compare percentages in whole numbers.

Calculate percentage increases and decreases in multiples of 5%, estimate using fractions and decimals, recognise common fraction-decimal-percentage equivalences, and work with simple ratio and direct proportions.

units.title: Measures: money, simple interest and discounts
units.description: Calculate simple interest and discounts in multiples of 5%, then interpret the result in a straightforward money context.
units.generationNotes: Use fictional money examples only. Restrict interest and discounts to multiples of 5%. Clearly distinguish the interest or discount from the final amount. Do not give financial product advice, recommend borrowing, or present this as personal financial guidance.

objectives.text: Calculate simple interest in multiples of 5% on amounts of money.
Calculate discounts in multiples of 5% on amounts of money.

units.title: Measures: converting units and using scales
units.description: Convert related units for length, weight, capacity, money and time, then use a simple scale on a map or drawing.
units.generationNotes: Keep conversions within the same measurement system. Include only one conversion step per item unless the item explicitly practises a connected two-step problem. For map or drawing scales, provide all information needed and state the units; do not rely on a diagram the learner cannot see.

objectives.text: Convert in the same system between units of length, weight, capacity, money and time.
Recognise and make use of simple scales on maps and drawings.

units.title: Shape and space: perimeter, area and volume
units.description: Calculate perimeter and area for straightforward composite rectangles, then calculate the volume of cubes and cuboids.
units.generationNotes: State every required dimension in the question. For composite rectangles, use a shape that can be explained fully in words or ASCII-free labelled dimensions; do not require an unseen image. Include units in each answer and explanation, and distinguish square units from cubic units.

objectives.text: Calculate the area and perimeter of simple shapes, including those that are made up of a combination of rectangles.
Calculate the volumes of cubes and cuboids.

units.title: Shape and space: properties, 3-D views and angles
units.description: Describe 2-D shape properties, interpret simple 3-D representations, and measure or use angles to describe position and direction.
units.generationNotes: For plans, elevations and nets, describe all relevant faces and dimensions in the question rather than assuming a visual. Include a symmetry or relative-angle concept and a direction or measured-angle context. Do not claim a learner has drawn or measured something when the activity is text-only.

objectives.text: Draw 2-D shapes and demonstrate an understanding of line symmetry and knowledge of the relative size of angles.
Interpret plans, elevations and nets of simple 3-D shapes.
Measure angles in degrees and use angles when describing position and direction.

units.title: Data: representing and grouping information
units.description: Read and choose tables, charts and graphs for discrete data, then group data and represent it clearly for a purpose.
units.generationNotes: Use compact fictional data sets that can be read in plain text. Cover a bar chart, pie chart or line graph concept and a grouped-data decision. Never ask learners to infer values from an unprovided image; give the values in a table or describe the graph precisely.

objectives.text: Represent discrete data in tables, diagrams and charts, including pie charts, bar charts and line graphs.
Group discrete data and represent grouped data graphically.

units.title: Data: mean and range
units.description: Find the mean and range of a small set of quantities, and choose the statement that describes what each measure tells you.
units.generationNotes: Use small, complete data sets with no ambiguous rounding. Include an interpretation distinction: mean describes an average, range describes spread from lowest to highest. Explanations must show the total and division for a mean, and identify the highest and lowest values for a range.

objectives.text: Find the mean and range of a set of quantities.

units.title: Data: probability and equally likely outcomes
units.description: Use the probability scale from impossible to certain, compare likelihoods, and express simple equally likely outcomes as fractions.
units.generationNotes: Use transparent, equally likely fictional outcomes such as coloured counters or fair spinners with fully stated sections. Cover the 0-to-1 probability scale, a likelihood comparison, and a fraction probability. Do not use real-world risk claims or assume outcomes are equally likely unless explicitly stated.

objectives.text: Understand probability on a scale from 0 (impossible) to 1 (certain) and use probabilities to compare the likelihood of events.
Use equally likely outcomes to find the probabilities of simple events and express them as fractions.
